extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and patent examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for a later‑filed U.S. (or international-designating-US) application to claim the benefit/priority of an earlier-filed provisional, nonprovisional, or international application under 35 U.S.C. §§ 119(e), 120, 121, 365(c), and 386(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely filing for provisional benefit (35 U.S.C. 119(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonprovisional application (or international application designating the United States) claiming benefit of a prior-filed provisional application must be filed not later than twelve months after the provisional application's filing date, subject to specified exceptions and restoration provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the 12-month day falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or Federal holiday in D.C., filing may be on the next business day (35 U.S.C. 21(b)). The benefit may be restored for filings up to two months late (i.e., up to 14 months) under PCT Rule 26bis.3 or upon petition under 37 CFR 1.78(b) if the delay was unintentional; a petition filed on or after May 13, 2015 must be filed in the subsequent application. See MPEP § 211.01 and 37 CFR 1.78(a)/(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior-filed application must be entitled to a filing date and required fees paid
rubrics_metrics.description: The prior-filed application relied upon for benefit must be entitled to a filing date under the applicable rules (e.g., 37 CFR 1.53(b)/(c)/(d) or PCT Article 11) and the basic filing fee for that prior application must have been paid within the applicable time period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For provisionals: entitled to a filing date per 37 CFR 1.53(c) and the basic provisional filing fee per 37 CFR 1.16(d) must have been paid within the time in 1.53(g). For nonprovisionals and international applications, follow the cited provisions (37 CFR 1.53(b)/(d), PCT Article 11, 37 CFR 1.1023). If a provisional was abandoned for failure to pay the basic fee, applicant may revive the provisional under 37 CFR 1.137; if grantable, acceptance should indicate the fee is deemed paid for 1.78(a)(2) compliance. Form paragraph 2.40 may be used to notify applicant when prior-filed app lacks filing date or fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventorship overlap requirement (same inventor or common joint inventor)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application claiming benefit under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) or 120 must name the inventor or at least one joint inventor named in the previously filed application or provisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If inventorship differs, correction may be required (see MPEP §§ 201.06, 602.01(c), 1412.04). Even with proper inventorship overlap, the later-filed application must still meet written description support under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) to be entitled to the earlier date (see MPEP § 211.05).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to the prior-filed application must be made and identified
rubrics_metrics.description: A later-filed application claiming benefit must contain, or be amended to contain, a reference to each prior-filed application identifying it by provisional application number (series code and serial number) or by application number/international application number and filing date as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the later-filed application is a nonprovisional application, the reference must be included in an Application Data Sheet (ADS) per 37 CFR 1.76(b)(5). For pre-September 16, 2012 nonprovisionals, the first sentence(s) of the specification following the title satisfied the requirement. For international/national stage matters, include the proper international numbers and filing dates. Cross-references to other related applications may be made when appropriate, but do not include cross-references in the ADS to applications for which benefit is not claimed. See 37 CFR 1.78(a)(3), (d)(2) and MPEP § 211.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits for submitting the reference (4‑month / 16‑month rules and national-stage specifics)
rubrics_metrics.description: The reference to the prior-filed application must be submitted during the pendency of the later-filed application and also within specific additional time windows: generally the later of four months from the actual filing date of the later-filed application or sixteen months from the filing date of the prior-filed application for 35 U.S.C. 111(a) applications; national-stage and 35 U.S.C. 371 entries have parallel but distinct time calculations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the later-filed application is a nonprovisional entering national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371, the reference must be submitted within the later of four months from national stage commencement or sixteen months from the provisional filing date, or comparable four-month triggers tied to the national-stage initial submission. Time limits do not apply to certain older applications (e.g., filed before Nov. 29, 2000). Failure to timely submit the reference is considered a waiver unless exception procedures apply (see paragraphs (b)/(c)/(e)). See 37 CFR 1.78(a)(4), (d)(3) and MPEP § 211.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delayed claims accepted only if unintentionally delayed and petition requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim for benefit presented after the applicable time period may be accepted only if the delay in presenting the reference was unintentionally delayed, and a petition to accept the unintentionally delayed claim must be filed with required items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For 35 U.S.C. 119(e) provisional benefit (delayed filing of the subsequent application): the petition (filed on or after May 13, 2015 in the subsequent application) must include the reference required by 119(e) (in ADS unless previously submitted), the petition fee per 37 CFR 1.17(m), and a statement that the delay was unintentional; the Director may require additional information. For delayed presentation of the reference itself under 119(e) or under 120/121/365(c)/386(c), the petition to accept an unintentionally delayed claim must be accompanied by the required reference (unless already submitted), the petition fee, and a statement that the delay was unintentional (for 120/121/etc., a statement that the entire delay between the due date and the filing date was unintentional). The Director may request more information where the unintentional nature is in question. See 37 CFR 1.78(b),(c),(e) and MPEP § 211.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation and accuracy statement for prior-filed non-English provisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: If the prior-filed provisional application was filed in a language other than English and an English translation and a statement that the translation is accurate were not previously filed in the provisional application, the applicant will be notified and given time to file the translation and statement in the provisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If notice is mailed in a pending nonprovisional, a timely reply in the nonprovisional must include confirmation that the translation and statement were filed in the provisional or the ADS must eliminate the reference to the provisional; otherwise the nonprovisional will be abandoned. The translation and statement may be filed in the provisional even if it has become abandoned. Form paragraph 2.38 can be used to notify applicant. See 37 CFR 1.78(a)(5) and MPEP § 211.01(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to provide transition statement for March 16, 2013 effective date issues
rubrics_metrics.description: If a nonprovisional application filed on or after March 16, 2013 claims the benefit of an application filed prior to March 16, 2013 and also contains (or contained at any time) a claim having an effective filing date on or after March 16, 2013, the applicant must provide a statement to that effect within a specified time period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement must be provided within the later of four months from the actual filing date of the later-filed application, four months from entry into the national stage as set forth in 37 CFR 1.491, sixteen months from the filing date of the prior-filed application, or the date a first claim with an effective filing date on or after March 16, 2013 is presented. Exceptions apply where earlier-filed applications already contain such statements or when applicants reasonably believe no such claims were present. See 37 CFR 1.78(a)(6),(d)(6) and MPEP § 211.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types and entitlement of prior-filed nonprovisional/international applications for 120/121/365(c)/386(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: To claim benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, 365(c), or 386(c), each prior-filed application must name the inventor (or a joint inventor) named in the later-filed application and must be an application entitled to a filing date as an international application, international design application, or a nonprovisional application under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) that meets the filing-date rules and fee requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically: (i) an international application entitled to a filing date per PCT Article 11 and designating the U.S.; (ii) an international design application entitled to a filing date per 37 CFR 1.1023; or (iii) a nonprovisional under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) with entitlement to a filing date per 37 CFR 1.53(b)/(d) and payment of the basic fee per 37 CFR 1.16 during pendency. See 37 CFR 1.78(d)(1) and MPEP § 211.01(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference must identify relationship (continuation/divisional/CIP) and continued prosecution application as specific reference
rubrics_metrics.description: References to prior-filed nonprovisional/international applications claiming benefit under 120/121/etc. must identify the application number (series and serial), international application number and filing date, or international registration number and filing date, and must identify the relationship of the applications (i.e., whether the later-filed application is a continuation, divisional, or continuation-in-part).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request for a continued prosecution application under 37 CFR 1.53(d) is the specific reference required by 35 U.S.C. 120 to the prior-filed application. The identification of an application by application number is the identification of every application assigned that number necessary for a specific reference required by 35 U.S.C. 120. See 37 CFR 1.78(d)(2)-(4) and MPEP § 211.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications with patentably indistinct claims — elimination and double patenting concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Where two or more applications filed by the same applicant/assignee contain patentably indistinct claims, elimination of such claims from all but one application may be required absent good and sufficient reason for retention. If an application/patent under reexamination and another application naming different inventors are owned by the same person and contain patentably indistinct claims, the Office may require statements about common ownership or prior inventorship; double patenting rejections may be applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may require the applicant/assignee to state whether the claimed inventions were commonly owned or subject to an obligation of assignment to the same person on the effective filing date (as defined in 37 CFR 1.109) or, if not, indicate which named inventor is the prior inventor. Even if commonly owned, patentably indistinct claims may be rejected under the doctrine of double patenting in view of such commonly owned or assigned applications or patents under reexamination. See MPEP § 211.01(f)-(g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time periods are generally not extendable (subject to limited statutory/treaty exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The time periods set forth for making benefit claims and submitting references are not extendable in general.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, they are subject to 35 U.S.C. 21(b) (and 37 CFR 1.7(a)), PCT Rule 80.5, and Hague Agreement Rule 4(4). Petitions and restoration procedures exist in certain limited circumstances (e.g., unintentionally delayed filings/petitions under 37 CFR 1.78). See 37 CFR 1.78(k) and MPEP § 211.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner actions when claims are not entitled to benefit of earlier filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: If the claims in the later-filed application are not entitled to the benefit of an earlier filing date (e.g., prior-filed application does not satisfy requirements), the examiner should notify applicant and treat the application as having the actual filing date for prior art searching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner may use form paragraph 2.09 and other appropriate form paragraphs to notify applicant that conditions for receiving the benefit were not satisfied. The examiner should conduct a prior art search based on the actual filing date of the application rather than the earlier filing date and may use an intervening reference in a rejection until the applicant corrects the benefit claim or demonstrates entitlement. See MPEP § 211.01 summary and related form paragraph guidance.
